The IApplicationPaths interface is likely defined in the Emby.Server.Implementations project or one of the referenced projects. Since I cannot read those files directly, I will create a minimal interface in the test that matches the properties used in the LogEnvironmentInfo method, but I will make sure to cast the TestApplicationPaths instance to that interface type in the test to avoid the compile error.

I will also fix the string.StartsWith calls in the assertions to specify StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase to avoid the CA1310 warning.

I will resubmit the test with these fixes.

```csharp
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Linq;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using Xunit;
using Moq;
using Jellyfin.Server.Helpers;

namespace Jellyfin.Server.Tests.Helpers
{
    public class StartupHelpersTests
    {
        private class TestApplicationPaths : IApplicationPaths
        {
            public string ProgramDataPath => "/program/data";
            public string LogDirectoryPath => "/log/dir";
            public string ConfigurationDirectoryPath => "/config/dir";
            public string CachePath => "/cache/path";
            public string TempDirectory => "/temp/dir";
            public string WebPath => "/web/path";
            public string ProgramSystemPath => "/program/system/path";
        }

        [Fact]
        public void LogEnvironmentInfo_LogsExpectedInformationIncludingApplicationPath()
        {
            // Arrange
            var loggerMock = new Mock<ILogger>();
            IApplicationPaths appPaths = new TestApplicationPaths();

            var loggedMessages = new List<(string message, object[] args)>();

            loggerMock.Setup(l => l.Log(
                LogLevel.Information,
                It.IsAny<EventId>(),
                It.Is<It.IsAnyType>((v, t) => true),
                It.IsAny<Exception>(),
                (Func<It.IsAnyType, Exception, string>)It.IsAny<object>()))
            .Callback(new InvocationAction(invocation =>
            {
                var state = invocation.Arguments[2];
                var formatter = invocation.Arguments[4] as Func<object, Exception, string>;
                var message = formatter?.Invoke(state, null);
                var stateProperties = state.GetType().GetProperty("Values")?.GetValue(state) as IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<string, object>>;
                var args = stateProperties?.Select(kvp => kvp.Value).ToArray() ?? Array.Empty<object>();
                loggedMessages.Add((message ?? "", args));
            }));

            // Act
            StartupHelpers.LogEnvironmentInfo(loggerMock.Object, appPaths);

            // Assert
            Assert.Contains(loggedMessages, m => m.message.StartsWith("Environment Variables:", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
            Assert.Contains(loggedMessages, m => m.message.StartsWith("Arguments:", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
            Assert.Contains(loggedMessages, m => m.message.StartsWith("Operating system:", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
            Assert.Contains(loggedMessages, m => m.message.StartsWith("Architecture:", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
            Assert.Contains(loggedMessages, m => m.message.StartsWith("64-Bit Process:", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
            Assert.Contains(loggedMessages, m => m.message.StartsWith("User Interactive:", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
            Assert.Contains(loggedMessages, m => m.message.StartsWith("Processor count:", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
            Assert.Contains(loggedMessages, m => m.message.StartsWith("Program data path:", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
            Assert.Contains(loggedMessages, m => m.message.StartsWith("Log directory path:", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
            Assert.Contains(loggedMessages, m => m.message.StartsWith("Config directory path:", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
            Assert.Contains(loggedMessages, m => m.message.StartsWith("Cache path:", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
            Assert.Contains(loggedMessages, m => m.message.StartsWith("Temp directory path:", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
            Assert.Contains(loggedMessages, m => m.message.StartsWith("Web resources path:", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
            Assert.Contains(loggedMessages, m => m.message.StartsWith("Application directory:", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) && m.args.Contains(appPaths.ProgramSystemPath));
        }
    }

    // Minimal interface stub for IApplicationPaths to compile the test
    public interface IApplicationPaths
    {
        string ProgramDataPath { get; }
        string LogDirectoryPath { get; }
        string ConfigurationDirectoryPath { get; }
        string CachePath { get; }
        string TempDirectory { get; }
        string WebPath { get; }
        string ProgramSystemPath { get; }
    }
}
```

The test fails to compile because the method expects the real IApplicationPaths interface from the MediaBrowser.Common.Configuration namespace, but my test defines a local interface with the same name, causing a type mismatch.

I will apply the `wrapper_interface` refactor to the LogEnvironmentInfo method's IApplicationPaths parameter so that it accepts an interface IApplicationPathsWrapper that I can implement in the test. This will allow me to inject a test double for the appPaths dependency.

<tool>apply_refactor(transform=wrapper_interface)</tool>

The wrapper_interface refactor is not available due to a missing Roslyn tool. I will try the make_virtual refactor on the LogEnvironmentInfo method to allow subclassing and overriding it in a test subclass, so I can intercept the logger calls.

<tool>apply_refactor(transform=make_virtual, method=LogEnvironmentInfo)</tool>
